turn1.explanation: The unit fires on clause and list punctuation (commas, periods, semicolons) in documents about ships, boats and other maritime vessels. It appears to carry a 'ship/vessel topic' signal at each sentence or list boundary, not on the topic words themselves.
turn1.evidence: Most of the strongest windows are ship or boat texts: SeaArk boats, Karadeniz powerships and power barges, a cruise-ship casino review, Swedish historic ship listings, flying boats and V.Ships crew. Example 5 (anchor-electronics.com) and probably Example 8 ('anchor' text) look like a lexical spillover from 'anchor'. In all of them the peaks sit on commas and full stops, while ship and boat tokens stay near zero. The weaker windows (news broadcasting, a CT radiology report, a court docket) show the same punctuation firing at lower values with no visible ship context.
turn1.missing_data: Full-document context for the weaker non-maritime examples, to confirm whether ship or anchor terms appear outside the window. Also matched comparisons of punctuation activation in maritime versus non-maritime documents.
